description: Turns MPE from a MIDI keyboard into polyphonic control voltages, one polyphonic channel for each MIDI channel, with its own envelope shaping the pressure

params.text: Sets the first MIDI channel read, 1 to 16
Sets how many MIDI channels are read, and so how many channels every output carries; the count is trimmed so it never runs past MIDI channel 16
Sets how slowly the volume falls away after a note held for less than about an eighth of a second; the higher the setting the longer the tail
Sets how slowly the volume falls away after a note held for more than about a fifth of a second; the higher the setting the longer the tail
Pulls pitch bend towards whole semitones: at the left the bend passes through untouched, and turning it right narrows the band between semitones until the bend snaps from one to the next
Bends the note-on velocity curve, from one raised in its middle at the left to one hollowed in its middle at the right
Lengthens the fall after a short note in proportion to the modulation value, so a note played further up the key holds on longer

outputs.text: 10V while a note is held on that MIDI channel, on one polyphonic channel per MIDI channel; with Gate Velocity Mode on it carries the note-on velocity instead
The pressure of the note through the envelope, taken from channel aftertouch, polyphonic aftertouch or control change 11, raised to the power of 1.3 and halved
The note's pitch with the pitch bend added, one volt per octave, with 0V for MIDI note 60
Control change 1 or 74 on that MIDI channel, 0 to 10V, smoothed
The note's pitch without any pitch bend, one volt per octave, with 0V for MIDI note 60
The pitch bend on its own, one volt per octave; a full bend is 4V, which is 48 semitones

notes: nothing comes out until a MIDI device is chosen with the button at the top of the panel. That button is not a parameter, so clicking it for help gives nothing.
the panel marks the outputs W, X, Y and Z after the MPE dimensions: W the gate, X the three pitch jacks, Y the modulation and Z the volume.
the green lamp at the bottom lights while the volume is arriving as 14-bit control change, that is control change 11 with control change 43 carrying its lower half.
menu: Gate Velocity Mode — puts the shaped note-on velocity on the gate output in place of a flat 10V
Preserve Pitch after Note-Off — keeps the pitch bend applied once the note has ended, instead of dropping the pitch output back to the plain note
Panic — clears every note, gate, bend and modulation and re-opens the MIDI port
